title: Node-health 🟡/🔴 warning surface (Ev_Warning_Raised/Ev_Warning_Cleared) has zero test coverage
evidence: core/crisis.odin:53-59: "prev := c.node_health[i] / if level != prev { / c.node_health[i] = level / if level == .Healthy { / emit(state, tick, Ev_Warning_Cleared{node = t.node_id[i]}) / } else { / emit(state, tick, Ev_Warning_Raised{node = t.node_id[i], level = level})". Grep of every 'expect event' in demos/*.dem: only grace_started, run_lost, packet_arrived, forecast_issued, crisis_triggered, run_won — no warning_raised/warning_cleared. No crisis_test.odin exists (core test files: determinism, flow, flow_edge, health, qos, rng, topology). grep 'health_strain_threshold_pct|health_critical_threshold_pct|node_health' in core/*_test.odin: no hits.
detail: The strain ladder (Strained→Critical→Cleared) is emitted and even parseable by the harness (demo_parse.odin valid_event_name lists both), but no unit test or demo asserts either event or the threshold boundaries. The entire warning surface is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add crisis_test.odin asserting threshold-boundary transitions (Strained/Critical/Cleared event emission) and add 'expect event warning_raised' to a surge demo capture window.

title: E9 drop ladder (per-lane queue-depth shed, newest-first) has zero coverage — no test or demo touches Queue_Overflow
evidence: core/flow.odin:451-456: "if idx_in_lane > int(bal.queue_drop_depth) { / // per-lane queue bound: beyond the depth, packets shed / // newest-first (the Godot prototype's actual behavior — / // its comment claimed oldest-first; the comment lied) / drop_packet(f, idx, .Queue_Overflow, &arrived)". data/balance.json:15: '"queue_drop_depth": 60'. grep 'Queue_Overflow|queue_drop_depth' across core/ harness/ demos/ returns only types.odin:26, catalog.odin:95/359, flow.odin:451/455 — no test file, no demo; no demo asserts 'expect event packet_dropped'.
detail: The overload shed ladder (the E9 behavior named in the review's priority list) is implemented but never asserted: no unit test verifies shed order or the depth bound, and no demo checks packet_dropped. A broken ladder would only trip the T1 golden, never a semantic check.
recommended_fix: Add a flow unit test flooding a contended pipe and asserting .Queue_Overflow drops shed Best-first at the depth bound; add 'expect event packet_dropped' to a demo.

title: Port limits: only the basic-4 unit test; mid-8/high-16 boundaries and the E2E router_ports_full rejection are never exercised
evidence: demos/draw_and_reject.dem: "at 100ms draw_pipe router house_a standard -> ok ... at 900ms draw_pipe host router wide -> ok" — 6 successful draws onto the boot router. data/node_types.json:7: '{ "id": "router_mid", ..., "port_capacity": 8 }'. core/topology_test.odin test_port_limits: "// canon #14: a basic router has 4 ports — one per connected pipe" spawning router_basic and asserting the 5th pipe returns .Router_Ports_Full — basic-4 only. No demo asserts 'router_ports_full'.
detail: draw_and_reject is the edit-contract demo yet never reaches the cap: 6 pipes on the boot MID router (8 ports). Canon #14's mid-8 and high-16 caps are never boundary-tested and the E2E rejection path is never asserted; only basic-4 is unit-pinned.
recommended_fix: Extend test_port_limits to mid-8/high-16 caps and add a draw-to-full '-> router_ports_full' intent to draw_and_reject (or a growth-router draw in surge_basics).

title: qos_dial demo asserts only 'expect hash stable' — the claimed lane behavior has no semantic assertion
evidence: demos/qos_dial.dem:8-12: "at 500ms set_triage router streaming -> ok / at 700ms set_priority router-house_a streaming -> ok / run 20000ms / capture at 8000ms, 16000ms / expect hash stable". Contrast demos/flow_basics.dem:9: "expect event packet_arrived within 0ms..5000ms". The only demos asserting flow events are flow_basics (packet_arrived), error404 (grace_started, run_lost), surge_basics (forecast_issued, crisis_triggered, run_won).
detail: The demo claims 'streaming wins contention THROUGH it' but asserts nothing about delivery — no packet_arrived/packet_dropped expectation. The T1 golden pins the trajectory (a regression breaks the hash) but never states what correct behavior is; semantics rest on unit tests only.
recommended_fix: Add an 'expect event packet_arrived' window plus a no-starvation/drop assertion to qos_dial.dem so the dial's effect is asserted, not just pinned.

title: verify_replay hardcodes bare=false: the map-fixture flag is dead code, so a future bare demo replays on the six-node fixture
evidence: harness/replay.odin:116-120: "// the fixture flag is carried by the demo; bare demos don't reach here / // with commands, but replay the same way / bar := false / _ = bar / replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(len(live_hashes)), false, &fails)". All 7 demos use 'map demo_six_nodes' (parse_demo defaults map_fixture = "demo_six_nodes"), so no current demo hits it — the log header does not record the fixture.
detail: The replay gate rebuilds the six-node fixture unconditionally and the log never records the fixture; a future 'map bare' demo would replay against the wrong topology. Today it fails loudly on hash divergence, so it is a latent harness trap, not a silent one.
recommended_fix: Record the map fixture in the log header and thread it through verify_replay/run_replay, or assert in run_demo that bare-fixture demos skip the replay gate.
